condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

1.1. Achieved. Based on the report provided by national coordinator of the Project attached to the Audit documents of the project we can strongly admit that 30 % of NHRAP was completed. The mid-term M&E of the implementation of NHRAP by international expert planed to be delivered in 2023. 1.2. Achieved. The reporting form/M&E form of the NHRAP which was developed in October, 2021 by international expert of the project David Johnson was actively used by national partners - Working Group of IAC in 2022 in the process of development of the Draft of the new NHRAP for 2022-2028. All comments, recommendation and form itself were useful indeed to develop tangible Draft of the NHRAP for 2022-2028. This new NHRAP is expected to be adopted by the government in the beginning of 2023. 1.3.The activity was delivered last year. 1.4. The activity is planned for the next year according to Project Document. 1.5. Achieved. Ashgabat, 21-22 July 2022: UNDP and the Government of Turkmenistan conducted the two-day workshop – Discussion of the Preliminary Analysis of the National Legislation for Compliance with the Provisions of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), in UN Building. The workshop gathered all members of the Working Group of the Interdepartmental Commission on the implementation of international obligations of Turkmenistan in the field of human rights and international humanitarian law (Interdepartmental Commission). The workshop was delivered by the international expert Mr. Thomas Baranovas. 1.6. Achieved. The activity was delivered last year instead of this year. 2.1. Achieved. There is no invitation received from the UN Treaty Bodies. Therefore, in compliance with the Project Document activities, for 4 members of the Working Group of IAC introductory and study trip to Finland was arranged. The goal of the Turkmenistan mission to Finland was to learn the social protection system of Finland and how the UPR recommendation and ICESCR implemented in the country. All practical knowledge gained will be implemented in the country to develop social protection system of the country and contribute to the effective implementation of Turkmensitan`s human rights obligations. Moreover, the gained knowledge will be used by the member of Working Group if IAC during the Dialogue with the UN Treaty Bodies in 2023. 2.2. Achieved partially. The expert was duly hired, the agenda was drafted and all preparatory steps were taken and the event was planned to be delivered in the beginning of December. However, due to the fact that the approval of the travel of the Turkmenistan delegation to Finland was received late from the government of Turkmenistan and the mission was planned well before with relevant arrangements with the MFA of Finland it was arranged to the beginning of December with postponement of the workshop on developing the National Report of Turkmenistan within The Fourth Cycle of the Universal Periodic Review on Human Rights planned for December 7-8 was postponed to February 2023. 3.1. 100 copies of the Collection of HR Conventions translated into TKM language were printed and disseminated. 100 copies were downloaded to CDs and disseminated. Also the Collection will be uploaded to the web-sites of UNDP and Institute of State, Law and Democracy of Turkmenistan by the end of 2022. 3.2. Achieved. Ashgabat, 12 April 2022: UNDP and the Government of Turkmenistan convened a workshop in a hybrid format on the Constitution of Turkmenistan as the guarantor of human rights and freedoms. The event gathered representatives of Milli Gengesh of Turkmenistan, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Prosecutor`s Office, Judicial system, other ministries, and agencies including civil society organizations from Mary, Balkan, Dashoguz, Lebap velayats and Ashgabat city. 3.3. Achieved. The Special working group to develop and introduce HR educational courses at the ministries and agencies was established. Roadmap on development and establishment of HR courses at the Institutes and Universities of Turkmenistan was developed as a result of the workshop for the Working group delivered by international expert of the project. 3.4. Achieved. The activity was delivered last year.
